clue.text: Joint in which sophisticated parents get seasonable snow

indicators.note: in which says the next piece goes inside the joint just named

parts.note: the wrist is a joint of the arm
hi-tech means technically sophisticated
mas are mothers, so parents

explanation.surface: Somewhere in a smart joint, cultured parents get snow at just the right time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Joint' a place to eat or drink; it is a body joint, and 'in which' sends the sophisticated word in just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names snow falling at Christmas, just what the season calls for.

clue.text: See 9
… in Rome and 6 in Rome, fowing in Rome

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: '… in Rome and 6 in Rome, fowing in Rome (5)': the opening is an ellipsis standing for the clue's own number and 'fowing' is a misprint, so the definition and first piece cannot be quoted honestly.
annotationWithheld.clue: … in Rome and 6 in Rome, fowing in Rome

clue.text: P45, instrument for cheat

parts.note: a P45 is the UK form given on leaving a job; to 'get your cards' is to be dismissed, so cards
the harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A dismissal form and a musical instrument are offered up as a swindler's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: A P45 is the tax form a UK employee gets on leaving a job; 'getting your cards' means being sacked, so P45 gives CARDS.
explanation.definitionFit: A card sharp is a swindler who cheats at card games, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: William in America, under cover with backing

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece placed under comes after
with backing tells us to read the covering word from back to front

parts.note: fur is an animal's covering
US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: Someone called William is living in America undercover, with secret support.
explanation.walkthrough: William Rufus was William II of England. 'with backing' turns FUR into RUF, and 'under' puts US below it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Rufus was the nickname of King William II of England, so the name stands for a William.

clue.text: Dispatch always covers church school occasion

indicators.note: covers means the speed word goes round the church abbreviation

parts.note: dispatch can mean haste, speed
ay (aye) is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A message that is always sent around a church becomes a school's big event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispatch' looks like a message sent but means haste. A speech day is a British school's annual prize-giving.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech day is a yearly event at a British school with speeches and prize-giving, so an occasion there.

clue.text: Muslim leader, no leader for Jihad possibly

definitions.text: Muslim leader, no leader for Jihad possibly

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Muslim
possibly signals the remaining letters may be arranged in another way
no leader for means the first letter of the next word is dropped

explanation.surface: A Muslim leader is described as possibly not one to lead a holy war.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the figure itself: 'no leader for' drops the J, and 'possibly' rearranges what is left of Jihad behind Muslim's initial.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mahdi is the redeemer expected in Islamic belief, a Muslim leader figure.

clue.text: Scout leader, rugged but too thin

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter, here of Scout

parts.note: craggy means rugged, rough-featured

explanation.surface: A scout leader is rugged, but also rather too skinny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scout leader' reads as a troop leader; it is just the first letter of Scout.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraggy means thin and bony, so overly thin.

clue.text: Improved P45 with information about former employees and fish

indicators.note: about says the information word goes round the former word

parts.note: gen is informal British for information
old means former
hands are workers, employees
hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: A better dismissal form comes with details on ex-staff and some fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A P45 is the UK form handed to someone leaving a job, so an improved one comes with a big pay-off. GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden handshake is a generous payment on leaving a job, a dismissal made better.

clue.text: Carnivore of little weight

definitions.meaning: a meat-eating animal, here the snow leopard
a small unit of weight, one sixteenth of a pound

explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is the snow leopard, a meat-eater, and also a small imperial weight.

clue.text: Whistleblower at home with female of course

parts.note: a referee blows the whistle, so ref
res is short for residence, a home
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Someone who exposed wrongdoing is at home with a woman, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistleblower' suggests an informer; it is the referee with the whistle. 'of course' looks like 'naturally' but describes a kind of course.
explanation.definitionFit: A refresher is a short training course that updates skills, so it is a type of course.

clue.text: Give hell to girl then give her P45

parts.note: Dis is the Roman underworld, hell
miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: Someone gives a girl hell and then sacks her.
explanation.walkthrough: A P45 is the UK form given when a job ends, so giving one means sacking.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss an employee is to sack her, which comes with handing her a P45.

clue.text: P45 made of hessian?

definitions.meaning: the UK form handed to a sacked employee stands for dismissal
hessian is a coarse jute cloth used for sacks

explanation.definitionFit: Sacking is dismissal, when the P45 is given, and also coarse sack cloth such as hessian.

clue.text: Welsh town not on top

definitions.meaning: below, underneath, in the poetic short form

explanation.definitionFit: Neath is a town in south Wales, and 'neath is the poetic short form of beneath, under.

clue.text: Aspirations about half the games not playing in Ramadan

indicators.note: about places the two aspirate letters round the other pieces

parts.note: an aspiration is an H sound, so two of them are HH

indicators.note: half keeps only the first half of the word for the games

parts.note: the Games are the Olympics

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of not are put into play in a new order

explanation.surface: Breathy sounds go round as half the games are cancelled during the fasting month.
explanation.walkthrough: Aspirations are H sounds, so 'about' wraps two of them round half of the Olympics and the letters of 'not' put into play by 'playing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar, kept as a sacred month of fasting.

clue.text: Austria, say, turned right out of churchyard

indicators.note: turned signals the remaining letters are turned about into a new order
out of says the letter for right is taken from the word churchyard

explanation.surface: Someone turned right and left a churchyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes one R from CHURCHYARD; 'turned' rearranges the rest. Austria was an archduchy within the Holy Roman Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria was historically ruled by archdukes, so it is an example of an archduchy.

clue.text: Prison first allowed to painter

parts.note: can is slang for prison
A is first, as in A1 or grade A
let means allowed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prisoner is first allowed out to paint.
explanation.walkthrough: Canaletto was the Venetian painter of city views.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaletto was an eighteenth-century Venetian artist famed for views of Venice.

clue.text: Saucer successful last year?

definitions.meaning: last year's winner keeps the trophy cup

explanation.definitionFit: A saucer holds a cup, and the winner of last year's contest holds the cup until the next.

clue.text: Wine helps to blur the effect of skidding

indicators.note: to blur means the letters of wine helps are smudged into a new order

explanation.surface: A glass of wine seems to help make things fuzzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheelspin is a wheel turning without grip, what happens when tyres skid.

clue.text: Rooms for naval officers and Yorkshiremen, say, beaten in battle?

indicators.note: say tells us to hear the words as spoken, here in a Yorkshire voice

parts.words: Rooms for naval officers and Yorkshiremen
parts.note: a wardroom is the officers' mess on a warship; Yorkshiremen pronounce room nearer to rum

explanation.surface: Navy officers' rooms and a gang of Yorkshiremen are thrashed in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire is a county in northern England where 'room' can sound like 'rum'. 'beaten' turns from defeated to struck, as a drum is.
explanation.definitionFit: A war drum is beaten in battle to rouse troops or signal attack.

clue.text: City slicker's little friend with his tail for his head

indicators.text: with his tail for his head
indicators.note: the word's last letter replaces its first letter

parts.note: a puppy is a young dog, man's little friend

explanation.surface: A town smoothie's young pet has its tail where its head should be.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is'. 'with his tail for his head' puts PUPPY's last letter Y in place of its first P.
explanation.definitionFit: A yuppy is a young urban professional, a smart city type.

clue.text: Fairies raised by tree surgeon?

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: an elf is a fairy creature
fay is an old word for a fairy

explanation.surface: Little magical folk were brought up by a man who looks after trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the whole run ELF FAY upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The yaffle is the green woodpecker, which drills into trees, so jokingly a tree surgeon.

clue.text: Type of acid for people with a lot of rodents

parts.note: a race is a people

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all of the next word

parts.note: mice are rodents

explanation.surface: An acid suits people who keep many rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the last E from MICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Racemic acid is a form of tartaric acid, so the word names a type of that compound.

clue.text: Disgraced artist's tree

indicators.note: the 's stands for has: the words hold the tree inside them

explanation.surface: A shamed painter owns a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The cedar is an evergreen conifer, a type of tree.

clue.text: Part of cycle unwelcome to house seeker

definitions.meaning: the linked metal loop driving a bicycle
in British house buying, a line of dependent sales that can collapse

explanation.definitionFit: A bicycle has a drive chain, and a chain of linked property sales can delay a home buyer.

clue.text: Student, supposing him to be posh, has a flying start

parts.note: L, the learner plate, stands for a student
if means supposing
a toff is a posh person

explanation.surface: A student who thinks himself upper-class makes a quick start.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF is British slang for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Lift-off is the moment a rocket or aircraft leaves the ground, the start of a flight.

clue.text: Encouraged with P45?

definitions.meaning: given the UK form handed out on dismissal

explanation.definitionFit: Fired means stirred up or inspired, and also sacked, which brings the P45.

clue.text: Common insect keeps debt collector from getting P45?

indicators.note: keeps says the insect holds the collector inside

parts.note: the red ant is a common insect
a dun is someone who demands payment of debts

explanation.surface: A common insect stops a debt collector being sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: A P45 is the UK form given to someone losing a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Being made redundant means losing one's job, the time a P45 is handed over.

clue.text: Lakeland water from river for female reactionary

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

indicators.note: reactionary means turning back, so the word for female reads backwards

parts.note: a lady is a female

explanation.surface: A lake in the north of England comes from a river, for a conservative woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Rydal Water is a small lake in England's Lake District (Lakeland).
explanation.definitionFit: Rydal Water is a lake in the Lake District, so a body of Lakeland water.

clue.text: "Halt!" "Left wheel!" etc, with P45?

definitions.meaning: the UK form handed out on dismissal

explanation.definitionFit: Marching orders are military drill commands, and getting one's marching orders means being dismissed.
